column1: # Manually curated genealogy evidence. Blank relationships are intentional when evidence is insufficient.

column16: taxonomy_notes_override
Ferrari identifies the 166 Inter as its first road car; later Inter succession is corroborated by specialist histories.
Touring version of the 195 S; the short-lived model sits between the 166 and 212 Inter.
Ferrari states that the 250 Europa took over from the 212 Inter.
Ferrari's historical and editorial year is retained independently from the effective 1952 production or delivery start.
Ferrari explicitly says it took over from the 212 Inter.
Ferrari calls the 375 America heir to the 342 America.
Ferrari says the model was developed from the 250 Europa; later derivatives do not form one unambiguous successor chain.
Ferrari calls this the first model in the berlinetta series.
No successor is assigned because the available Ferrari evidence does not explicitly establish one.
Ferrari describes it as an open 250 GT Berlinetta; LWB and SWB subseries are combined in the source snapshot.
Two-seat Pininfarina spider associated with the 250 GT road range.
Accepted human decision: the 250 GTO is recorded as a derivative of the SWB competition berlinetta.
No predecessor or successor is forced without explicit evidence.
Ferrari's historical article explicitly says the 275 GTB replaced the 250 GT Lusso.
Accepted human decision: road-homologated competition derivative of the SWB; not a Lusso successor.
Ferrari explicitly identifies the Lusso replacement and the later four-cam iteration.
Ferrari calls it the spider version and notes shared chassis systems; its body and tune differ materially.
No predecessor or successor is forced without explicit evidence.
Ferrari calls the 365 GTB4 an evolution of the 275 GTB4.
Ferrari states the 365 GTC design was basically similar to the last 330 GTCs.
Open counterpart of the 330 GTC; treated as a derivative and not a core generation.
A distinct very-low-volume luxury spider; no evidenced direct successor is assigned.
Accepted human decision: the 550 link is spiritual; the direct commercial successor was the mid-engined 365 GT4 BB.
No direct successor is asserted; the 365 GTC/4 belongs to the 2+2 family in this taxonomy.
Open derivative of the 365 GTC; distinct from the 365 GTS4 Daytona Spider.
Ferrari identifies it as the convertible version of the 365 GTB4; production began later than its 1969 debut.
Accepted human decision: spiritual successor to the 365 GTB4 and direct commercial successor to the F512 M.
Open limited derivative of the 550 Maranello.
The M denotes a modified Maranello; treated as evolution rather than a clean-sheet successor.
Convertible derivative of the contemporary 575M architecture.
Core front-engine V12 berlinetta; special and open versions are derivatives.
Limited special-series derivative rather than a new core generation.
Limited open derivative of the 599 family.
Core successor in Ferrari's front-mid-engine V12 berlinetta sequence.
Limited high-performance derivative of the F12berlinetta.
Core berlinetta succeeded officially by the 12Cilindri.
Open derivative of the 812 Superfast.
Limited special-series berlinetta derived from the 812 Superfast.
Open special-series derivative of the 812 Competizione.
Ferrari explicitly presents it as the successor to the 812 Superfast.
Open derivative launched alongside the 12Cilindri berlinetta.
Ferrari states that the final fifty 250 GT 2+2 cars received the 330 America engine; the transitional model retained the outgoing body and chassis.
The purpose-built 330 GT 2+2 directly replaced the short-lived transitional 330 America.
Ferrari identifies the 365 GTC4 as continuing where the 365 GT 2+2 left off.
Ferrari explicitly calls it successor to the 365 GT 2+2 and predecessor of the 365 GT4 2+2.
Ferrari describes a brand-new design following the GTC4; the 400 series later replaced it.
Ferrari describes it as a more powerful development of the 365 GT4 2+2.
Automatic-transmission parallel derivative; Ferrari says the 400 series replaced the 365 GT4 2+2.
Fuel-injected evolution of the carburetted 400 GT.
Automatic derivative of the injected 400 GTi; Ferrari also explicitly says it succeeded the 400 Automatic.
Ferrari says the 412 replaced the 400i; official history identifies it as the 456 GT predecessor.
Ferrari explicitly identifies the 412 as predecessor and the 456M as the closely related replacement.
Automatic-transmission derivative of the 456 GT.
Ferrari explicitly calls the 456M an evolution of its traditional 2+2 interpretation.
Automatic-transmission derivative within the evolved 456M range.
Ferrari presents it as continuation of the great 2+2 tradition; direct succession is corroborated by model chronology and specialist histories.
First production Ferrari with four-wheel drive; the GTC4Lusso officially evolved its formula.
Ferrari says it replaced and evolved the FF; Purosangue later builds on the formula but changes category and layout.
V8 rear-wheel-drive derivative; moved out of the V12 family while retaining its GTC4Lusso base model.
Ferrari calls it the first four-door four-seater and says it builds on the FF/GTC4Lusso formula; this supports conceptual rather than direct succession.
Same 250 GT 2+2 body and chassis with the new four-litre V12; a transitional evolution directly replaced by the new 330 GT 2+2.
Presented in 1971 but production began in June 1973. BB is the historical Berlinetta Boxer name; technically the engine is a 180-degree V12 rather than a true boxer.
Capacity and drivability evolution of the 365 GT4 BB on the same core template.
Fuel-injected update of the 512 BB; the substantially redesigned Testarossa is its direct heir rather than a mild evolution.
Ferrari calls it heir to the 512 BBi; the 512 TR retained its conceptual framework with extensive evolutionary changes.
Ferrari describes the 512 TR as an evolution of the Testarossa and the F512 M as its modified final development.
Final modified flat-12 model; Ferrari explicitly states that the front-engined 550 Maranello replaced it commercially.
Competition derivative prepared from the 512 BB by dealers to factory instructions with aerodynamic chassis engine and weight changes.
Presented in 1973 under the Dino marque; Ferrari says the Dino name ended after 1976 and the GT4 was Ferrari-badged until the Mondial replaced it in 1980.
Italian-market two-litre V8 derivative sharing the 308 GT4 body; presented in November 1974 and catalogued by Ferrari under 1975.
Ferrari explicitly calls it the replacement and successor to the 308 GT4; it marks the completed transition from Dino to Ferrari branding.
Four-valve update of the Mondial 8 with otherwise closely retained body and architecture.
Open 2+2 derivative of the Quattrovalvole; unveiled to the press in September 1983 and officially shown the following January.
Restyled and enlarged-engine evolution of the Quattrovalvole coupe.
Open derivative updated in parallel with the 3.2-litre coupe.
Longitudinal-engine and transverse-gearbox evolution of the Mondial; no later successor is assigned.
Open derivative using the Mondial T longitudinal-engine transverse-gearbox layout; no later successor is assigned.
Ferrari records at least two 1965 prototypes reworked and lightened for racing followed by a small customer series in 1966.
Competition version of the front-engined 365 GTB4; the source snapshot year denotes the first competition-series chronology.
Track research derivative based on the Enzo Ferrari; no homologated racing succession is implied.
Track research derivative based on the 599 GTB Fiorano; its continuity from FXX is retained as an alternative spiritual relation.
Ferrari explicitly describes the FXX K research programme car as based on its first hybrid road car; XX continuity is recorded separately.
Open derivative of the 849 Testarossa and direct range replacement for the SF90 Spider.
Daytona SP3 shares the Icona programme with Monza SP1/SP2; no predecessor-successor connection is recorded.
Atomic model name for chassis 0744 at its 1958 Spa debut; its later installation of a Type 141 engine formerly used by the 335 S is an example-level modification rather than a separate 335 model row.
